The problem with silicon is that it's very big. If you want to make faster and faster chips, you need to make smaller and smaller circuits, and pack them closer and closer together.

Human brains (and the brains of every single life form) are made out of carbon-based processors called neurons. Not only does biological computing vastly exceed mechanical computing in this way, but these neurons also INTERFERE with each other. They do the exact thing that right now is the biggest bottleneck to making better and faster chips out of silicon. Each individual neuron compensates for other neurons, and they all work together to create what is called a "neural field" which stabilizes all the signals.

With the technology currently available, you would need a computer the size of the moon to reach the same processing power as a human brain (and you would never even reach certain benchmarks you need carbon to do).
